partes.title: Mensajes y anuncios: datos concretos
partes.descripcion: En el examen escuchas mensajes de voz y anuncios cortos y eliges el dato exacto: una hora, un precio, un lugar o un número. Lee la pregunta antes de escuchar y cuidado: suelen mencionar varios números o lugares, pero solo uno responde a la pregunta.

tareas.audio: Hi Tom, it's Sarah. The party is on Saturday, at my flat. Please don't come at six, because I'm at work until then. The party starts at seven. See you on Saturday!
tareas.pregunta: ¿A qué hora empieza la fiesta?
tareas.why: Sarah dice "The party starts at seven"; las seis es la hora en que termina de trabajar. "Flat" es británico; en inglés americano se dice "apartment".

tareas.audio: Good morning, shoppers. Today apples are cheap! A bag of apples is only two pounds. Bananas are one pound fifty. Thank you for shopping with us.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuánto cuesta una bolsa de manzanas?
tareas.why: "A bag of apples is only two pounds". Una libra cincuenta es el precio de los plátanos: es la trampa.

tareas.audio: Hello, this is a message for Anna. Your English class is not in room four today. It is in room nine, on the first floor. Thank you.
tareas.pregunta: ¿En qué aula es la clase de Anna hoy?
tareas.why: Hoy la clase no es en el aula cuatro sino en la nueve. Ojo: en Gran Bretaña "first floor" es el primer piso sobre la planta baja (en EE. UU. sería "second floor").

tareas.audio: Hi Mum, it's Leo. I can't visit you on Tuesday, because I have to work. Can I come on Thursday? I'm free all day. Bye!
tareas.pregunta: ¿Qué día quiere visitar Leo a su mamá?
tareas.why: Leo no puede el martes ("Tuesday") porque trabaja; propone el jueves ("Thursday"). "Mum" es británico; en EE. UU. es "Mom".

tareas.audio: Hello, this is a message from Doctor Green's surgery. Please call us back on oh one two three, four five six, seven eight nine. Thank you.
tareas.pregunta: ¿A qué número tiene que llamar?
tareas.why: Los números se dicen uno por uno y "oh" significa cero. "Surgery" en inglés británico es el consultorio del médico (en EE. UU. "doctor's office").

tareas.audio: Attention, please. The train to Oxford leaves from platform three at ten fifteen. Platform three, ten fifteen. Thank you.
tareas.pregunta: ¿De qué andén sale el tren?
tareas.why: "Platform three" es el andén; diez ("ten fifteen") es parte de la hora de salida, no el andén. En EE. UU. se suele decir "track" en vez de "platform".

tareas.audio: Thank you for calling the Regal Cinema. Tonight's film, The Long Road, starts at twenty to nine. Tickets are nine pounds for adults and six pounds for children. Popcorn is five pounds.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuánto cuesta la entrada para un niño?
tareas.why: "Six pounds for children". Nueve libras es la entrada de adulto y cinco las palomitas. "Cinema" es británico; en EE. UU. se dice "movie theater".

tareas.audio: Hi Daniel, it's Mark from the office. The meeting tomorrow was at half past nine, but the manager can't come until eleven. So we're meeting at quarter to twelve now, in the small room. Sorry about the change!
tareas.pregunta: ¿A qué hora es ahora la reunión?
tareas.why: "Quarter to twelve" = las doce menos cuarto (11:45). Las 9:30 era la hora anterior y a las 11:00 solo llega el jefe.

tareas.audio: Hi Kate, it's Jo. About Sunday: we can't meet at the park, because it's going to rain. Let's meet at the café next to the library instead. You know, the one opposite the bank. See you there!
tareas.pregunta: ¿Dónde van a encontrarse Kate y Jo?
options: En el café junto a la biblioteca
tareas.answer: En el café junto a la biblioteca
tareas.why: Jo cambia el parque por el café "next to the library". El banco solo sirve de referencia: el café está enfrente ("opposite").

tareas.audio: We are sorry to announce that the twelve twenty service to Manchester is delayed by twenty-five minutes. This train will now leave at twelve forty-five from platform six.
tareas.pregunta: ¿A qué hora sale ahora el tren a Manchester?
tareas.why: El tren de las 12:20 tiene 25 minutos de retraso, así que sale a las 12:45 ("twelve forty-five"). En los anuncios británicos "service" significa el tren o el bus de ese horario.

tareas.audio: Hello, this is a message from Fit Life Gym. Your membership ends on the fifteenth of March. If you renew before the tenth, it costs only thirty pounds a month, not thirty-five. Call us or come to reception.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuánto cuesta al mes si renueva antes del día 10?
tareas.why: Antes del día diez cuesta treinta libras; treinta y cinco es el precio normal y quince es la fecha en que termina la membresía.

tareas.audio: Hello, this is Rosa's Restaurant. I'm calling about your booking for Friday. You asked for a table for six at eight o'clock, but we're full at that time. We can give you the same table at half past eight or at nine. Please call us back to let us know.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Qué horas le ofrece el restaurante?
tareas.why: A las ocho está lleno; ofrecen "half past eight or nine". El seis es el número de personas. "Booking" es británico; en EE. UU. se dice más "reservation".

tareas.audio: Good afternoon, visitors. Please note that the museum will close at half past five today, thirty minutes earlier than usual, because of a private event. The café on the ground floor will stop serving at a quarter to five. The gift shop, however, will stay open until the museum closes. We apologise for any inconvenience.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Hasta qué hora está abierta hoy la tienda de regalos?
tareas.why: La tienda abre "until the museum closes", y hoy el museo cierra a las cinco y media. Las 4:45 es la hora del café y las 6:00 el cierre habitual. "Apologise" es la ortografía británica (EE. UU.: "apologize").

tareas.audio: Hi, it's Emma from the travel agency, about your trip to Edinburgh. The hotel you wanted costs a hundred and twenty pounds a night, which is well over your budget. I've found another one, a bit further from the centre, for ninety-five pounds, and breakfast is included, so I'd go for that. There's also a hostel at forty pounds, but you said you wanted a private bathroom, so I don't think it's right for you. Let me know what you think.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuánto cuesta por noche el alojamiento que Emma recomienda?
tareas.why: Emma dice "I'd go for that" del hotel de noventa y cinco libras. El de ciento veinte es muy caro y el hostal no tiene baño privado. "Centre" es británico (EE. UU.: "center").

partes.title: Monólogos: la idea principal
partes.descripcion: Escuchas a una persona hablar de un tema y eliges su idea principal o la razón que da. No te quedes con la primera palabra que coincida: presta atención a "but", "the main reason" o "that wasn't it", que suelen indicar lo que la persona realmente quiere decir.

tareas.audio: I walk to work every day. It's only twenty minutes from my house. I have a car, but parking in the city centre is really expensive, so I leave it at home. That's the main reason. Walking is good exercise too, of course.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuál es la razón principal por la que va a pie al trabajo?
options: Porque aparcar en el centro es caro
Porque su médico se lo dijo
tareas.answer: Porque aparcar en el centro es caro
tareas.why: Dice "That's the main reason" justo después de hablar del precio del parking. Sí tiene coche ("I have a car").

tareas.audio: My favourite day of the week is Sunday. On Saturdays I work in a shop, so I'm always tired. But on Sundays I get up late, and I cook a big lunch for my family. We all sit together and talk for hours. That's the best part for me.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Qué es lo que más le gusta del domingo?
options: No ir a trabajar a la tienda
Comer y conversar con su familia
tareas.answer: Comer y conversar con su familia
tareas.why: "That's the best part" se refiere a sentarse juntos a hablar. Levantarse tarde también lo menciona, pero no dice que sea lo mejor. "Favourite" es la ortografía británica (EE. UU.: "favorite").

tareas.audio: I started learning the guitar last year. It wasn't for my job, and it wasn't for school. My grandfather played the guitar, and when he died, he left me his old one. I wanted to play his songs, so I started lessons.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Por qué empezó a aprender guitarra?
options: Para tocar las canciones de su abuelo
Porque lo necesitaba para su trabajo
Porque se lo pedían en la escuela
tareas.answer: Para tocar las canciones de su abuelo
tareas.why: "I wanted to play his songs": quería tocar las canciones de su abuelo. Niega explícitamente el trabajo y la escuela.

tareas.audio: People often ask me why I moved from London to a small village. Everyone thinks it was for the cheaper houses, and yes, houses are cheaper here, but that wasn't it. I was working from home anyway, and I realised I was spending my whole day indoors. Here I can go for a walk in the countryside at lunchtime. Being close to nature was what I really needed.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuál fue la verdadera razón de su mudanza?
options: Que las casas son más baratas
Que consiguió trabajo en el pueblo
Querer estar cerca de la naturaleza
tareas.answer: Querer estar cerca de la naturaleza
tareas.why: Trampa típica: menciona las casas baratas pero dice "that wasn't it". La razón real: "Being close to nature was what I really needed". Ya trabajaba desde casa.

tareas.audio: I've been a nurse for fifteen years. The pay isn't great, and the night shifts can be really hard, especially in winter. But when a patient who arrived very ill walks out of the hospital smiling, I remember why I do this job. That feeling is worth more than any salary.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Qué quiere decir sobre su trabajo de enfermería?
options: Que ayudar a los pacientes compensa las dificultades
Que el sueldo es lo más importante
Que quiere dejar los turnos de noche
tareas.answer: Que ayudar a los pacientes compensa las dificultades
tareas.why: Reconoce los problemas (sueldo, turnos), pero con "But..." llega a su idea principal: esa satisfacción "is worth more than any salary".

tareas.audio: Our town decided to close the main street to cars at weekends. At first, some shop owners were worried that they'd lose customers. In fact, the opposite happened. Families now come to walk around, children play safely, and the cafés have put tables outside. Most shops say they're selling more than before.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuál es la idea principal?
options: Cerrar la calle a los coches ha beneficiado al comercio
Los niños ya no pueden jugar en la calle
tareas.answer: Cerrar la calle a los coches ha beneficiado al comercio
tareas.why: La preocupación de los comerciantes era solo al principio; "the opposite happened" y ahora venden más. "At weekends" es británico (EE. UU.: "on weekends").

tareas.audio: I used to buy a new phone every year, as soon as a new model came out. I don't do that anymore. It isn't really about the money. I read an article about how much rubbish old phones create, and how the materials are taken from the ground. Now I keep my phone until it actually stops working.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Por qué ya no compra un teléfono cada año?
options: Porque no le gustan los modelos nuevos
Por el impacto en el medio ambiente
tareas.answer: Por el impacto en el medio ambiente
tareas.why: Descarta el dinero ("It isn't really about the money") y habla de la basura y los materiales: es por el medio ambiente. "Rubbish" es británico (EE. UU.: "trash" o "garbage").

tareas.audio: When I set up my bakery, I assumed the hardest part would be the long hours, getting up at four every morning. Surprisingly, I got used to that within a few weeks. What nearly made me give up was the paperwork: taxes, health inspections, licences. Nobody warns you that running a small business means spending half your time as an accountant rather than doing what you love.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Qué fue lo más difícil de abrir la panadería?
tareas.why: Esperaba que madrugar fuera lo peor, pero dice que se acostumbró ("got used to that"). Lo que casi la hace rendirse fue "the paperwork". "Licence" es la ortografía británica del sustantivo (EE. UU.: "license").

tareas.audio: There's a widespread belief that teenagers today don't read. My experience as a school librarian suggests otherwise. What's changed is not whether they read, but what they read and how. They'll get through long fantasy series on their phones, or follow online discussions for hours. If we only count printed novels from the school reading list, of course the numbers look bad. The problem lies in how we measure reading, not in the young people themselves.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuál es la idea principal de quien habla?
options: El problema está en cómo se mide la lectura
Los adolescentes de hoy ya no leen
Los jóvenes deberían leer más novelas impresas
tareas.answer: El problema está en cómo se mide la lectura
tareas.why: Menciona la creencia de que no leen solo para rechazarla ("suggests otherwise"). Su conclusión: "The problem lies in how we measure reading".

tareas.audio: I turned down a promotion last month, and my colleagues thought I'd lost my mind. The salary was considerably higher, and the title would have looked great on my CV. But the role involved travelling abroad almost every week, and with two young children, I simply wasn't prepared to miss that stage of their lives. Money can be earned later; those years can't be repeated.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Por qué rechazó el ascenso?
options: Porque el sueldo no era suficientemente alto
Porque no quería perderse la infancia de sus hijos
Porque sus compañeros se lo aconsejaron
tareas.answer: Porque no quería perderse la infancia de sus hijos
tareas.why: El sueldo era mucho mayor y sus compañeros no lo entendieron; la razón es no perderse "that stage of their lives". "CV" es británico (EE. UU.: "résumé").

partes.aptis: Parte 3 · él, ella o los dos
partes.title: Conversaciones: él, ella o los dos
partes.descripcion: Escuchas una conversación entre un hombre y una mujer y decides quién expresa una opinión: él, ella o los dos. Fíjate en expresiones de acuerdo ("I agree", "you're right") y de desacuerdo ("I see your point, but..."). A veces coinciden en una cosa y discrepan en otra.

tareas.audio: MAN: What shall we do on Saturday? WOMAN: I'd love to go to the beach. It's going to be hot and sunny. MAN: Hmm, I don't really like the beach. It's always so busy. I'd prefer to stay at home and watch a film. WOMAN: OK. Maybe I'll go with my sister, then.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién quiere ir a la playa el sábado?
tareas.why: Solo la mujer quiere ir ("I'd love to go to the beach"); el hombre prefiere quedarse en casa. "Shall we" y "film" son británicos (EE. UU.: "should we", "movie").

tareas.audio: WOMAN: Did you try the new Italian restaurant on King Street? MAN: Yes, I went on Friday. The pizza was nice, but it was very expensive. WOMAN: I agree. I paid twenty pounds for some pasta! The food is good, but it's too expensive for me. MAN: For me too. I won't go there often.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién piensa que el restaurante nuevo es caro?
tareas.why: Él dice "it was very expensive" y ella "I agree... too expensive for me". Cuando uno dice "I agree" o "me too", la respuesta suele ser "Los dos".

tareas.audio: WOMAN: So, now the company lets us choose, are you going to work from home or come into the office? MAN: Home, definitely. I save an hour and a half on the train every day, and I can concentrate much better without people chatting around me. WOMAN: I see your point, but I tried it last year and I felt really lonely. I need to see my colleagues, so I'll be in the office every day. MAN: Well, maybe I'll come in on Fridays to say hello to everyone.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién prefiere trabajar desde casa?
tareas.why: El hombre dice "Home, definitely". La mujer se sintió sola y irá a la oficina todos los días. Que él vaya algún viernes no cambia su preferencia.

tareas.audio: MAN: Sophie keeps asking for a mobile phone. She's only ten. I really think she's too young. WOMAN: I used to think that too, but she walks to school on her own now. I'd feel much safer if she could call us. MAN: She could borrow mine on those days. I just worry she'll spend all day on it. WOMAN: We can set limits. Honestly, I think it's time.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién cree que Sophie ya debería tener móvil?
tareas.why: La mujer "used to think that too" (antes pensaba lo mismo), pero ahora dice "I think it's time". El hombre sigue creyendo que es muy pequeña. "Mobile phone" es británico (EE. UU.: "cell phone").

tareas.audio: WOMAN: So, what did you think of the film? MAN: The actors were brilliant, but honestly, three hours was far too long. I nearly fell asleep in the middle. WOMAN: Really? I thought the acting was a bit weak, actually. But you're right about the length. They could have cut at least forty minutes. MAN: Exactly. The story would have been much stronger.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién piensa que la película era demasiado larga?
tareas.why: No están de acuerdo sobre los actores, pero sí sobre la duración: ella dice "you're right about the length". La pregunta es solo sobre la duración.

tareas.audio: MAN: Our car is getting old. I've been reading about electric cars, and I think it's time we bought one. They're much cheaper to run. WOMAN: But they cost so much more to buy. And where would we charge it? We haven't got a garage. MAN: There are charging points at the supermarket, and the government gives you some money back. WOMAN: I'm still not convinced. I'd rather get a second-hand petrol car.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién está a favor de comprar un coche eléctrico?
tareas.why: El hombre propone comprarlo; la mujer "is still not convinced" y prefiere uno de gasolina. "Petrol" y "haven't got" son británicos (EE. UU.: "gas", "don't have").

tareas.audio: MAN: Did you see that the school is doubling the number of exams next year? WOMAN: I did, and frankly, I think it's a mistake. An exam just shows how a student performs on one particular morning, under pressure. Some of the brightest kids I teach go completely blank. MAN: I'm not so sure. Everyone feels the same pressure, so exams are still the fairest way to see what students have really learned. Coursework can be copied, and teachers' opinions aren't always fair. WOMAN: Then assess them in a variety of ways, rather than putting everything on a few tests.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién piensa que los exámenes no muestran bien lo que sabe un estudiante?
tareas.why: Ella critica los exámenes ("one particular morning, under pressure"). Él responde "I'm not so sure" y defiende que los exámenes son "the fairest way to see what students have really learned".

tareas.audio: WOMAN: I've just booked flights to Lisbon for thirty pounds. Isn't that amazing? MAN: It's great for your wallet, but I can't help thinking flights shouldn't be that cheap. The environmental cost isn't reflected in the price at all. WOMAN: Maybe, but if prices went up, only wealthy people could afford to travel. Is that fair? MAN: Then tax frequent flyers more heavily, not the family that flies once a year. But overall, yes, I'd make flying more expensive.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién opina que volar debería ser más caro?
tareas.why: Él lo dice claramente: "I'd make flying more expensive". Ella responde "Maybe, but...", que no es acuerdo: le preocupa que solo los ricos puedan viajar.

tareas.audio: MAN: The council is finally discussing the new cycling plan. WOMAN: About time. Every time I cycle to work, I feel like I'm risking my life. We desperately need proper, separate bike lanes. MAN: I don't cycle myself, but I completely agree. If more people felt safe on a bike, there'd be less traffic for those of us who have to drive. WOMAN: I doubt they'll ever agree on the budget, though. MAN: Oh, I'm more optimistic about that.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién cree que la ciudad necesita más carriles bici?
tareas.why: Aunque él no va en bici, dice "I completely agree" (por sus propios motivos: menos tráfico). Solo discrepan sobre el presupuesto. "The council" es el ayuntamiento local en Gran Bretaña.

tareas.audio: MAN: My nephew's just been accepted on an exchange programme in Japan. WOMAN: Lucky him. I had the chance to spend a year in Germany when I was at university, and I turned it down because I didn't want to leave my friends. I still regret it, to be honest. MAN: Really? I did a term in Spain, and while it was fun, I don't think it changed my life as much as people claim. I'd have been fine without it. WOMAN: Well, I often wonder how different things would have been.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Quién se arrepiente de no haber estudiado en el extranjero?
tareas.why: La mujer rechazó la oportunidad y dice "I still regret it". El hombre sí estudió fuera ("a term in Spain") y no se arrepiente de nada. "Programme" es la ortografía británica (EE. UU.: "program").

partes.title: Monólogos y entrevistas: opinión y actitud
partes.descripcion: Escuchas un monólogo o una entrevista más largos y eliges la opinión o actitud de quien habla. Las opciones incorrectas suelen ser ideas que sí se mencionan, pero que son de otras personas o que el hablante rechaza. Busca frases como "personally", "I don't share it" o "I'm now convinced".

tareas.audio: I run a small clothes shop, and lots of people told me I had to be on every social media app to survive. So I tried. I posted photos every day, made videos, and answered messages late at night. Some shop owners say it brings them loads of new customers. Honestly, in my case, it didn't. Most of my customers live nearby, and they come because a friend recommended us. Now I only post once a week, and I spend that time talking to people in the shop. For a business like mine, I think personal contact matters far more than being online.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Qué opina sobre las redes sociales para su tienda?
options: Son menos importantes que el trato personal
tareas.answer: Son menos importantes que el trato personal
tareas.why: "Imprescindibles" es lo que le decían otros, y los clientes nuevos es lo que dicen otros comerciantes ("in my case, it didn't"). Su opinión: "personal contact matters far more".

tareas.audio: WOMAN: You've been running marathons for ten years. How do you feel about running with music? MAN: Well, a lot of runners say music helps them go faster, and there's some research that supports that. But personally, I find it takes me away from the experience. I like hearing my breathing and my feet on the road. And in a race, you need to hear what's happening around you. So I never use headphones, and I'd advise beginners to try without them first.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuál es la actitud del corredor hacia correr con música?
options: Cree que la música le ayuda a correr más rápido
Piensa que está prohibida en las carreras
tareas.why: Que la música ayuda a ir más rápido es lo que dicen otros corredores. Con "But personally..." da su opinión: "I never use headphones". No dice que esté prohibida.

tareas.audio: My parents were worried when I decided to study cooking instead of going to university. They thought it was a job with no future. I understand why they felt that way. The hours are long, and at the beginning the pay is low. But I've never been happier. I wake up every morning excited about work, and I learn something new every single day. For me, that's more important than having a degree.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cómo se siente respecto a su decisión?
options: Contento y seguro de haber elegido bien
tareas.answer: Contento y seguro de haber elegido bien
tareas.why: La preocupación es de sus padres y reconoce el sueldo bajo, pero dice "I've never been happier". Entender a alguien ("I understand why") no es compartir su opinión.

tareas.audio: MAN: Do you think machine translation will replace people like you? WOMAN: That's the question everyone asks. Some of my colleagues are genuinely frightened, and I understand why, since prices for simple jobs have fallen. But I'm not particularly worried. The machines are excellent for getting a quick idea of what a text says, and I use them myself. What they can't do reliably is judge tone, humour, or what a client really wants to say to a specific audience. I think the job will change rather than disappear, and translators who learn to work with these tools will be fine.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuál es la actitud de la traductora ante la traducción automática?
options: Tiene miedo de perder su empleo
Tranquila: la ve como una herramienta que cambiará su trabajo
Cree que las máquinas no sirven para nada
tareas.answer: Tranquila: la ve como una herramienta que cambiará su trabajo
tareas.why: El miedo es de sus colegas; ella dice "I'm not particularly worried" y usa las máquinas ("excellent for..."), así que tampoco cree que sean inútiles. "Humour" es británico (EE. UU.: "humor").

tareas.audio: I grew up in a small fishing town that's now one of the most popular holiday spots on the coast. People assume locals like me must hate the tourists, and I do know some who complain constantly about the crowds and the rents. But I'd be lying if I said I felt the same. Without visitors, half the shops would have closed years ago, and my own children wouldn't have summer jobs. What I would like is for the council to control holiday flats more strictly, so that young families can still afford to live here. So it's not tourism I object to; it's the lack of planning.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Qué opina sobre el turismo en su pueblo?
options: Odia a los turistas por las multitudes
Cree que no ha traído beneficios económicos
Lo valora, pero pide que se regule mejor
tareas.answer: Lo valora, pero pide que se regule mejor
tareas.why: Las quejas son de otros vecinos ("I'd be lying if I said I felt the same"). Reconoce beneficios y concluye: "it's not tourism I object to; it's the lack of planning". "Holiday flats" es británico (EE. UU.: "vacation rentals").

tareas.audio: WOMAN: Your company tried a four-day week last year. Was it a success? MAN: It depends who you ask. The staff loved it, obviously, and sick days went down noticeably. Our clients were less enthusiastic at first, because they couldn't reach us on Fridays, but we solved that with a rota. As for me, I'll admit I had my doubts at the start. I expected productivity to fall. It didn't. If anything, people wasted less time in meetings. So yes, I'm now convinced it works for us, although I wouldn't say it suits every type of business.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuál es ahora la opinión del hombre sobre la semana de cuatro días?
options: Está convencido de que funciona en su empresa, aunque no en todas
Cree que los clientes nunca la aceptarán
tareas.answer: Está convencido de que funciona en su empresa, aunque no en todas
tareas.why: Tenía dudas "at the start", pero ahora "I'm now convinced it works for us", con un matiz. El problema con los clientes se resolvió. "Rota" (turnos) es británico (EE. UU.: "schedule").

tareas.audio: As a football coach for under-twelves, I'm often asked whether competition is bad for young children. Some parents would like us to stop keeping scores altogether, so that nobody feels like a loser. I respect that concern, but I don't share it. Children know perfectly well who won, whether we write it down or not. Learning to lose, and to win without showing off, is part of growing up. What I do think is harmful is adults on the touchline shouting at the kids as if it were a professional match. That's the pressure I'd get rid of, not the scores.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Qué piensa el entrenador sobre la competición en el deporte infantil?
options: Habría que dejar de contar los goles
Es sana; lo dañino es la presión de los adultos
Los niños no se dan cuenta de quién gana
tareas.answer: Es sana; lo dañino es la presión de los adultos
tareas.why: No contar los goles es la idea de algunos padres ("I respect that concern, but I don't share it"). Él dice lo contrario de la opción tres: los niños saben quién gana. "Football" es británico (EE. UU.: "soccer").

tareas.audio: MAN: You've written a book about living without a car in a big city. Are you trying to convince everyone to sell theirs? WOMAN: Not at all, and I think that's a common misreading. For people in rural areas, or people with mobility problems, a car can be essential, and I'd never criticise them. My argument is narrower. In a city with decent public transport, owning a car is often a habit rather than a need. Most city cars sit parked almost all day. When I sold mine, I expected to feel restricted. Instead, I felt oddly free: less stress, more walking, more money. But I'm careful not to tell other people how to live.
tareas.pregunta: ¿Cuál es la postura de la autora?
options: Todo el mundo debería vender su coche
Vender su coche la hizo sentirse limitada
En una ciudad con buen transporte público, el coche suele ser un hábito, no una necesidad
tareas.answer: En una ciudad con buen transporte público, el coche suele ser un hábito, no una necesidad
tareas.why: Rechaza la primera interpretación ("Not at all"). Esperaba sentirse limitada, pero "Instead, I felt oddly free". Su tesis: "a habit rather than a need". "Public transport" es británico (EE. UU.: "public transportation").
